10ca55a7-0be9-49c9-a249-5a618966af91:
We were twelve in a cabin outside Dhaka
the winter snow came, absurd and soft,
sealing the road the festival van would use.
Arjun had promised word by evening:
whether the orchestra would play in the capital
or fold its music stands for good.
Meera, the youngest, held her violin unopened
in its case across her knees.
No one rehearsed. No one ate the rice.
By dusk the silence tuned itself to a single string,
and every face leaned toward the radio
the way a bow leans toward a note.
Arjun paced from the stove to the window,
his baton tucked behind one ear,
forgetting it was there.
Meera unlatched the case at last,
not to play, only to see the wood,
while snow kept falling past the glass.

and I arrive before the studio doors are open.
Jiayi, who farmed rice until the city reached her,
shapes a bowl as if she is patting soil flat.
Her daughter Ruoxi, home from surveying new roads,
measures the shelf with her eyes and calls it crowded.
They argue about price, about glaze, about space.
Neither notices how every bowl leans the same way,
a small tilt toward the window, like seedlings
looking for weather. I do not tell them.
Some knowledge belongs to the hands that made it,
and a guest should carry her cup carefully.
On the tram back, a man sells chestnuts from a tin,
and the steam fogs the glass in quick white circles.

like green stitches holding the slope together,

06136565-6e4d-4a50-9459-62dd5a2eb82f: When the last students had filed out of the classroom, I found Jomo still at the back desk, turning an old photograph over in his fingers. 9b3cf629-1b44-4181-a1d1-896e0c67b2c8: Marine biologists have long debated why some species of octopus exhibit such short lifespans, often dying within months of reproducing. 9bf0317a-8030-4ab8-a662-0659695a59c9: For decades, ethnomusicologists described the drumming of certain West African ensembles as largely improvised, noting that no two performances sounded identical and that lead drummers seemed to respond on the spot to the movements of dancers. Text 1
Art historians have long treated the sudden proliferation of self-portraits among Northern European painters in the sixteenth century as evidence of rising individualism, arguing that artists began to see themselves as worthy subjects independent of religious or aristocratic patronage. This shift, the argument goes, reflects a broader cultural turn toward valuing personal identity, one that anticipated Enlightenment notions of the autonomous self. The self-portrait, on this view, is fundamentally a declaration of the artist's individual worth.

Text 2
Guild records from the period reveal that self-portraits were frequently produced as demonstration pieces submitted to prospective patrons and guild councils to showcase technical skill, particularly in rendering skin tone, fabric, and light—qualities that were difficult to commission a model to sit for repeatedly. Painters often reused the same self-portrait composition across multiple submissions. This practice suggests that many self-portraits functioned primarily as professional advertisements of craft rather than as expressions of a newly emerging sense of individual identity.

9afe1001-ac09-4e42-8ab5-2fd3e3e30fed: Economic historians studying the decline of the transatlantic whaling industry in the mid-nineteenth century have debated whether the discovery of petroleum, and the resulting shift to kerosene for lighting, was the primary cause of whaling's collapse, or whether overhunting of whale populations had already made the industry unsustainable regardless of petroleum's emergence. I am Yuxuan, a nurse; I keep charts, not maps,
but I drew what he described on the back of one:
a footbridge, a willow, the dry stones he crossed in August

Every night since, I have walked a riverbed of linoleum,

Astronomers analyzing the orbits of distant icy bodies in the outer solar system have proposed that an undiscovered ninth planet, several times the mass of Earth, could explain why many of these objects share unusually clustered orbital paths. Computer simulations show that a massive planet's gravity, tugging steadily over millions of years, would naturally herd smaller bodies into the alignment observed today, making this hypothesis an elegant single explanation for the pattern.

Text 2

Other astronomers argue that the clustering could instead result from observational bias: telescopes are more likely to detect icy bodies in certain regions of the sky at certain times, which could create the appearance of alignment even if no such alignment exists in reality. Until wider, more uniform sky surveys are completed, they argue, it remains premature to invoke a new planet when a simpler explanation involving survey limitations has not yet been ruled out.

c0fd93c7-6fea-448b-a7bf-834c657781ed: When cities first began widening roads and adding lanes in the mid-twentieth century, planners assumed that increasing road capacity would permanently relieve traffic congestion. Text 1

Art historians examining the sudden popularity of chiaroscuro—the dramatic use of light and shadow—in seventeenth-century European painting often attribute the technique's rise to the influence of a small circle of innovative painters whose bold canvases circulated among wealthy patrons in major cities. According to this view, once influential collectors began commissioning works featuring stark contrasts of illumination, provincial painters imitated the style to attract similarly prestigious clients, and the technique spread outward from urban centers of artistic patronage to the wider continent within a few decades.

Text 2

The patronage-driven account of chiaroscuro's spread overlooks a simpler explanation rooted in materials rather than taste. Analysis of surviving pigments and canvases shows that this same period saw the wider availability of more affordable, stable dark pigments capable of rendering deep shadow without cracking or fading, alongside improved oil-based mediums that allowed for more precise gradations of light. Painters in provincial workshops, far from imitating fashionable urban patrons, appear to have adopted these techniques largely because the newly available materials simply made dramatic light effects easier and cheaper to produce reliably, regardless of who was commissioning the work.

Text 1
Marine biologists studying octopus cognition have observed that octopuses in captivity can learn to open jars, navigate mazes, and even recognize individual human caretakers. Some researchers argue that these behaviors indicate a form of intelligence comparable to that seen in mammals, despite the vast evolutionary distance separating cephalopods from vertebrates. They contend that intelligence may have evolved independently multiple times, and that octopuses represent a striking case of convergent cognitive evolution driven by the demands of a predator-rich environment.

Text 2
While octopuses undeniably display complex problem-solving behaviors, some skeptics caution against equating these abilities with mammalian-style intelligence. They point out that octopus nervous systems are radically decentralized, with most neurons located in the arms rather than a central brain, suggesting that what looks like learning may instead be a patchwork of localized reflexes and simple associative responses. These researchers argue that applying human-centric definitions of intelligence to such an alien nervous system risks overstating the animals' cognitive sophistication.

Cities that have implemented such fees, they note, have seen measurable declines in vehicle volume within months, along with increased bus and subway ridership as commuters shift away from driving.

Text 2
Critics of congestion pricing counter that the policy disproportionately burdens lower-income commuters who live in areas underserved by public transit and have no practical alternative to driving. Unlike wealthier residents who can absorb the fee or easily switch to transit, these commuters face a steep new cost simply to reach their jobs, meaning the policy may reduce traffic without providing every affected driver a genuine alternative.

cc0f9b20-6390-4e8f-a607-7850169e901b: Economists studying the collapse of the Dutch tulip market in 1637 have often described it as history's first speculative bubble, driven purely by irrational public enthusiasm for rare flower bulbs. c2446947-373c-430a-914b-968ec8687849: Coral reefs are often called the rainforests of the sea because of their extraordinary biodiversity, but they depend on a partnership that is far more fragile than most people realize. Coral polyps host microscopic algae called zooxanthellae within their tissues; the algae photosynthesize and share nutrients with the coral, while the coral provides the algae shelter and access to sunlight. When ocean temperatures rise even slightly above normal for an extended period, corals expel these algae in a stress response known as bleaching. Without the algae, the coral loses its primary source of nutrition and its vivid color, turning stark white. A bleached coral is not necessarily dead, and it can recover if temperatures drop quickly enough, but prolonged bleaching events often lead to widespread coral death and the collapse of the reef ecosystems that depend on it.

df42003e-fc27-4d1b-a1e7-722b46b91b67: Art historians long treated the Dutch flower still-life paintings of the seventeenth century primarily as displays of technical skill and wealth, noting that the exotic tulips, roses, and imported shells depicted in these canvases signaled their owners' prosperity during a period of expanding global trade. 831a4f88-9baf-4481-b907-5e2454933f94: For much of the twentieth century, urban planners in the United States treated highways as the default solution to traffic congestion, routing multi-lane freeways directly through the hearts of cities. Because mirror inspection is a standard sign of self-awareness, and because biting clients is a form of cheating that damages a cleaner's reputation, the researchers concluded that self-aware wrasse are better able to manage their reputations. The effect was strongest in wrasse collected from crowded reef sections, where clients are numerous.

Text 2
A separate team observed that cleaner wrasse vary widely in general boldness, a trait measurable by how quickly an individual approaches any novel object, whether a mirror, a plastic cube, or a colored disk. Bold wrasse lingered near all such objects equally long. The same bold individuals also tended to be the most experienced cleaners, having served more clients, and experienced cleaners are known to bite less because clients that are bitten stop returning.

aaa754d3-8eb9-43e3-b032-c7af004f5b6c: Tar and wet hemp, that was the smell of every crossing. I was fourteen the summer Budi began riding our barge up the estuary from the Cornish coast, always with a sealed parcel on his knees and never with a fare in his hand. Father had told me only that Budi had once pulled him from the water at Falmouth, and that I, Abena, was not to ask for money. Each morning I spliced the frayed end of our mooring line, and each evening it had worn through again against the iron ring. Budi watched me work the strands together and once offered to buy us new rope. I said the old one would hold, and he did not argue. By September the splice was thicker than the rope itself, a knot of patches I could have tied blindfolded. On his last crossing he set his parcel down, took the line from me, and wove one strand in himself before stepping ashore without a word.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Japanese art form of kintsugi repairs broken pottery by rejoining fragments with lacquer mixed with powdered gold.
- Kintsugi emerged in the late 15th century, reportedly after a shogun sent a damaged tea bowl to China for repair and was dissatisfied with the ugly metal staples used to fix it.
- Rather than hiding the damage, kintsugi highlights the cracks with shimmering gold seams, turning the break into a visible feature of the piece.
- The philosophy behind kintsugi is linked to the Japanese aesthetic of wabi-sabi, which finds beauty in imperfection and impermanence.
- Today, kintsugi is sometimes used as a metaphor in psychology and self-help writing to describe recovering from hardship and becoming stronger.
- Restoring a single bowl using traditional methods can take several weeks because the lacquer must cure in stages.
4fbf0008-9af6-458a-94ac-7828c732f938: A drawer of lead type slid open with a groan when Hamza needed the letter that, in our shared wall's language of knocks, meant come over. I had lived beside his printing press in Beirut for six years and knew its moods: the thump of the platen, the hiss of the ink roller, the mutter of a man who disliked every street map he had ever printed. That evening he spread a new one across his table and jabbed at the errors, a missing alley here, a renamed square there, until I, Mehreen, began to defend the city's mapmakers out of pure stubbornness. Then he traced a faint pencil line I had not noticed. It ran from my door to his, through the plaster. "This," he said, "they always leave out." I stopped arguing.
82bf419d-27e7-4be7-a3cf-3025fe34ad75: Seeds keep longer than people expect. By then the lease was ending, and the members had stopped coming to meetings, but no one said the word closing. Saga learned quickly. __She began writing a fourth line on each envelope, in small letters: where it could be planted next.__ Marit noticed and said nothing for a month. Then, one wet afternoon, she handed Saga the key to the oldest cabinet and a list of gardens across the city, some of them belonging to people she had not spoken to in years. The last jars left in a borrowed van, rattling down the Maasboulevard in the rain.
edd8620c-e2f9-49b1-ab4a-3ef1cbb78821: "Mend the heel, and I will pay you when we sing again," Stanislav said, setting one worn slipper on my counter. I hammered the heel while she hummed the opening bars, slightly flat, and waited for me to join. My throat was full of leather dust and doubt. f35cb418-822b-47ee-ba96-202a4c93a1a1: Nova climbed the mountain road above Marrakesh with an envelope of cash sewn into a coat lining, and the storm shut both of them inside Dalia's cabin for three days. Text 1
Marine biologists studying octopus cognition have proposed that these animals possess a form of intelligence comparable to that of many vertebrates, despite octopuses having a nervous system structured almost nothing like a mammal's. Two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are distributed throughout its arms rather than centralized in a brain, yet octopuses solve puzzle boxes, recognize individual human faces, and use tools such as coconut shells for shelter. Because these behaviors require flexible problem-solving rather than fixed instinctive responses, researchers argue that intelligence can evolve along radically different neural architectures and should not be measured by how closely an animal's brain resembles our own.

Text 2
While octopuses undeniably display impressive behavioral flexibility, some cognitive scientists caution against equating this flexibility with intelligence in the sense usually reserved for vertebrates. An octopus's arms can each act with a degree of autonomy, solving local problems like gripping or exploring without input from the central brain at all. This decentralization means that what looks like unified, deliberate problem-solving may actually be the aggregate of many semi-independent local reactions. Attributing a single, coherent intelligence to the whole animal, these researchers suggest, may overstate the case and obscure how differently octopus cognition is actually organized compared to centralized vertebrate brains.
728a69ce-3fdc-40f6-9f6f-508260e63483: On her first morning in Rotterdam, Hana stood in the customs line with her boots tied to her duffel bag, the same boots she had barely worn all last season on the bench. Months earlier she had told a reporter that she no longer knew what she was for. At the gate, Lars offered to carry the duffel, but Hana shook her head and slung it over her own shoulder, boots knocking against her back. 94638e74-3f8c-4755-bfa7-2c3342048b58: One can always see trouble who looks for it. 76ddaedb-a625-4e8d-abf0-74520fe553e1: Smoke from the chili oil stung Emiliano's eyes as he ladled broth at the noodle stall in Oaxaca, the stall he had rented from Anacleto for nineteen years. a0026856-5e37-413a-a3ed-5b7ce0a4f91b: Who else still remembered that our grandmother had called the house Two Ravens? Yona and I were selling what was left of it at the Saturday market, spreading her blankets and tin cups across a folding table in the wind. aa217e3e-f635-49cd-a831-927de09f4f9d: I was hired to translate for Yusuf, not to argue on his behalf. I rendered it into Arabic word for word, and Yusuf only folded the watch back into his handkerchief. On the walk home I kept turning the phrase over. A receipt proves a sale, I thought, but not an inheritance; a son could own a thing more fully than any buyer. The next week I returned alone and asked the clock-maker, in my plainest Spanish, whom the rule was meant to protect. He was quiet for a long while, then wrote his own name on a slip of paper and slid it across the counter as though it were a receipt.

3decd04c-1443-4e25-844b-ce2f18eb7c71: Economic historians studying the collapse of the Roman silver currency in the third century CE have generally attributed the debasement of coinage to wartime pressures, as emperors facing constant military campaigns needed to pay soldiers without raising taxes high enough to provoke rebellion. Reducing the silver content of coins allowed the state to mint more currency from the same amount of precious metal, effectively spreading a fixed supply of silver across a larger volume of coins. This practice, however, triggered inflation as merchants and soldiers alike recognized the diminished value of the debased coins and demanded more of them in exchange for goods and services. The resulting price increases further strained the imperial treasury, since the government now needed even more debased coinage to cover the same expenses, creating a self-reinforcing cycle that persisted for decades before currency reforms under Diocletian addressed the problem.
e2a7c59f-9d78-4eee-8ccb-62f61b158c00: When I moved back to Porto Alegre to care for my mother, I treated her beekeeper's yard as a list of chores. 4a8d0913-f7b3-490b-a3db-f72a7ec16e6b:
The chamber of the solitary student is peopled with immortal guests. He has friends who are always steadfast, who are never false, who are silent when he is weary, who go forth with him to his work, who await his return. In the literature of the world a grand society is open to all who choose to enter it.

Books are the chief food of our intellectual life.--There are men that have, indeed, done great things who have read but little. These have had their want of mental training compensated by their powers of observation and experience of life. But they have been for the most part exceptional men, and it is possible they might have done better if they had studied more.

267d2956-2f81-46e9-aeae-1d4a6e65a01b:
Text 1

Economic historians studying the collapse of small family farms in the early twentieth century often point to mechanization as the central cause. As tractors and mechanical harvesters became affordable, farms that could invest in this equipment achieved dramatically higher yields per worker, allowing them to undercut smaller neighbors on price. Within a generation, thousands of family farms that could not afford machinery were forced to sell their land to larger operations, consolidating agricultural production into far fewer, much larger farms than had existed before.

Text 2

Mechanization certainly reshaped agriculture, but focusing on machinery alone obscures the role that credit access played in determining which farms survived. Bank records from the period show that many small farms failed not because they lacked machinery outright, but because they were denied the loans needed to purchase it, while larger operations with more collateral secured favorable financing terms. Farms with equally modest yields but better banking relationships often survived the consolidation wave, while some mechanized but heavily indebted farms still failed when a single bad harvest made loan payments impossible to meet.
6473fcfd-9dcc-49d7-a2f0-eebea753e936: Economic historians examining the collapse of the Dutch tulip market in 1637 often point to the role of futures contracts, which allowed buyers to purchase bulbs that would not be delivered until the following growing season. When prices suddenly fell, many contract holders found ______ unable to pay the prices they had agreed to months earlier, and the resulting wave of defaults spread through the merchant community.
0f0df92c-80b8-44b2-9536-e0b969dd7a65:
ZEYNEP: (holding up a pocket watch) Your grandfather wound this every morning for forty years. And now you want to say goodbye to him with a speech?
APONI: A short one. Something proper. People expect it.
ZEYNEP: People expect sandwiches, too. (She snaps the watch open, grinning.) He'd have fallen asleep by your second sentence.
APONI: (laughing despite himself) He fell asleep at my graduation.
ZEYNEP: Twice. (Her grin fades. She listens to the watch, which has stopped.) He brought it here the week before he died. Asked me to fix it. I told him there was no hurry.
APONI: There wasn't.
ZEYNEP: (quietly, setting the watch on the counter between them) There was. I just didn't hear it. Wind it, child. Not for the speech. Let it run on the plateau a little longer than he did.

Text 1

Recent excavations of Bronze Age settlements in the eastern Mediterranean have uncovered large communal grain silos located at the center of villages rather than within individual households. Archaeologists studying these sites argue that this arrangement reflects a cooperative economic system in which grain surplus was pooled and redistributed by community leaders, reducing the risk that any single family would starve during a poor harvest. The consistent placement of these silos in public areas, often near ceremonial structures, further suggests that communal storage was tied to shared religious authority rather than private wealth accumulation.

Text 2

The interpretation of centrally located grain silos as evidence of egalitarian, cooperative economies deserves scrutiny. In several excavated villages, the silos nearest the ceremonial structures contained noticeably larger stores of grain than smaller silos scattered elsewhere, and skeletal remains from elite burials in the same period show better nutrition than those from ordinary households. This pattern is more consistent with a system in which local leaders controlled and unevenly distributed the communal surplus, using access to stored grain as a source of political power rather than a mechanism for protecting the whole community from famine.
8734f0bf-d3ac-4b0f-8112-11bab6a5acd5: The Atacama Desert in northern Chile is one of the driest places on Earth; some weather stations there have recorded almost no rain for decades. ______ the soil in many parts of the desert holds very little life, and scientists have used it to test equipment designed to search for microbes on Mars.

Do you remember the night bus to Kadikoy, Mr. Nikos? I doubt you knew I was sitting three rows behind you. For a whole term I had not said one word in your class, and you had stopped calling on me, which I took as a judgment. Then the bus stalled on the bridge, and you turned around and asked whether anyone had a pencil to lend a man who wanted to write down the lights on the water. I handed you mine. We talked until the engine caught again, mostly about poems I had never shown anyone. I think now that my silence was never indifference, only a kind of waiting. Here the rain has not stopped for days, and the gulls sleep on the ferry railings.

6c73bd5c-1406-4172-b0c7-6f504e2253bb: Astronomers tracking the orbital decay of satellites in low Earth orbit have observed an unexpected pattern tied to the eleven-year solar activity cycle. During periods of heightened solar activity, the sun emits more ultraviolet and X-ray radiation, which heats Earth's upper atmosphere and causes it to expand outward. Text 1

Art historians who study the shift from tempera to oil paint in fifteenth-century European workshops often emphasize technical advantages as the driving cause of the transition. Oil paint dries more slowly than tempera, allowing artists to blend colors gradually on the canvas and achieve subtle gradations of light and shadow that tempera's quick-drying surface made difficult. These historians argue that once painters recognized oil's capacity for richer modeling of form, workshops across Italy and northern Europe adopted the new medium primarily because it expanded what was technically achievable on canvas.

Text 2

Other historians studying the same transition argue that economic and social pressures, not technical capability alone, drove the shift to oil paint. They note that wealthy merchant patrons increasingly commissioned portable panel paintings for private homes rather than large frescoes for public spaces, and oil paint's durability and suitability for such panels made it commercially attractive independent of its blending properties. These historians contend that workshops adopted oil paint largely because patron demand for a new kind of artwork made the medium economically necessary, with its technical qualities serving as a secondary justification rather than the primary cause.

falling into a pot? Soren did,
old captain, on the promenade bench,
explaining his fish stew to the gulls
and to Leah, who had once hidden
in his hold among the potato sacks
and been found, and fed, and never sent back.
A handful of this. Enough of that.
Until it smells like the harbor at Newlyn
the morning after a storm.
Such instructions are useless, of course.

bd805953-26a3-4109-b37f-2041da2a1149: When urban planners in the mid-twentieth century began replacing streetcar networks with bus routes and expanded roadways, they typically justified the change by pointing to buses' lower upfront infrastructure costs and greater route flexibility, since buses did not require fixed rails or overhead electrical lines. __This flexibility, however, came at the cost of the very reliability that had made streetcars attractive to riders in the first place, because buses, unlike streetcars running on dedicated tracks, were subject to the same traffic congestion as private automobiles, making their arrival times far less predictable.__ Ridership data from several American cities that dismantled streetcar lines between 1940 and 1960 show a consistent pattern: bus ridership on former streetcar routes declined steadily in the years following conversion, even as overall urban population and automobile ownership were also rising, a confound that complicates any simple before-and-after comparison. a70180c2-9bb5-452d-8e6e-f52d17e70451: When city planners in the mid-twentieth century widened urban arterial roads to accommodate rising automobile traffic, they generally assumed that adding lanes would permanently ease congestion. Three rules my uncle Dewi kept at the loom:
count every thread, owe no one, trust no rival.
We owed the cooperative in Bologna
more than a winter's linen could repay,
and Nora, at the next loom, wove faster than us both.
He called her the competition. I called her nothing.
But when our warp snapped on the morning of the market,
it was Nora who knotted it, thread across thread,
her weft running sideways through our long, straight lines.
Warp holds still; weft crosses over.
Neither one alone is cloth.
By evening the bolt was finished, and my uncle,
counting, lost his place, and laughed, and counted again.

Urban planners in several mid-sized cities have recently championed the removal of highway overpasses that cut through downtown districts, replacing them with street-level boulevards. Proponents argue that these overpasses, built during a mid-twentieth-century push to accommodate automobile commuters, isolated neighborhoods from one another and depressed property values in adjacent areas. By tearing down the elevated structures, cities can reconnect fragmented districts, restore pedestrian access, and reclaim land for housing and retail development, generating new tax revenue that offsets the cost of demolition and reconstruction.

Text 2
Highway removal projects, however appealing in theory, often underestimate the disruption they cause to regional commuters who have structured their daily routines around quick automobile access to downtown employment centers. When cities eliminate elevated highways without first expanding public transit capacity, commuters are forced onto already congested surface streets, and travel times increase substantially for years during the transition period. Text 1
Urban planners advocating for congestion pricing argue that charging drivers a fee to enter busy downtown areas during peak hours is the most effective way to reduce traffic and encourage use of public transit. Cities that have implemented such schemes, they note, have seen measurable declines in vehicle volume and corresponding improvements in bus speeds and air quality. Proponents view congestion pricing as a market-based solution that internalizes the social costs of driving, ensuring that those who contribute most to gridlock bear a proportional share of the burden.

Text 2
Critics of congestion pricing counter that such fees disproportionately burden lower-income commuters who cannot afford to live near their workplaces and who often lack convenient access to public transit alternatives. While acknowledging that traffic reduction is a legitimate goal, these critics argue that flat fees are regressive, effectively pricing working-class drivers out of city centers while wealthier residents continue to drive unimpeded. "But as a daughter and a niece,
I pride myself on every piece
Of handiwork created;
While reveling in social chat,
Or listening to gossip flat,
My gain is unabated.

Seems to my mind a monarch born,
Worthy to lead a column;
I'll warrant he could talk and work,
And, neither being used to shirk,
Was rarely very solemn.

But must, before I go to bed.
Your idle precepts mocking,
Get out my needle and my yarn

Colette left the parcel on the fountain's dry lip,
the blue scarf I knitted through a Lyon winter,
folded back into its paper, unworn.
Forty years across one courtyard,
perhaps a hundred sentences between us.
The neighbors call it pride. I nearly did.
But the wool has taken on her lavender,
as if it slept a while in her drawer,
and tucked in the last fold, a strip of lace
worked in the pattern her mother taught us both,
Colette and Odile, nine years old, sharing one needle.
I sit beside the basin that holds no water
and count the stitches she added, row by row,
until the bells at Saint-Jean begin.

693194e5-bacc-4ff4-9b82-0e177d21d9e2: Art historians examining the workshop practices of the Dutch Golden Age painter Judith Leyster have noted a curious pattern in the archival record: several paintings once confidently attributed to her male contemporary Frans Hals were, after later technical analysis of brushwork and pigment layering, reattributed to Leyster herself. Notably, this pattern of misattribution was far more common for paintings that had been sold or exhibited without any signature visible, whereas paintings bearing Leyster's distinctive monogram were rarely misattributed, even when their style closely resembled that of other workshop members. Historians also found that unsigned works by several of Leyster's own male students were almost never mistakenly attributed to her, despite stylistic similarities, but were instead misattributed to Hals or left as "unknown master." Based on this evidence, historians have concluded that the earlier misattributions to Hals resulted primarily from ______
55c835ae-6c86-4a0b-bc2b-5c6ba536d57a: Glasgow rain had pooled on the lid of the rooftop water tank where Saoirse and I used to rehearse, back when we shared a stage at a cabaret on Sauchiehall Street. I climbed up there again last winter to scatter nothing in particular, just to look. Saoirse's mother had made a lamb stew for the cast every opening night, and she never wrote the recipe down. After she died, Saoirse and I tried for years to reproduce it, arguing over thyme and barley. __Once, Ronan, the old stagehand, told us we were cooking a memory, not a stew.__ We laughed at him then. Now Saoirse lives in Cork, and when she phones, we no longer talk about ingredients. We talk about the opening nights themselves. The tank hummed under my hand, full of a cold that never quite reached the street.
ea0b7a0e-5a01-4b72-b2ca-6d0547c0d584: After the irrigation pump exploded, Lars and Noor stood in the abandoned orchard outside Marrakesh, deciding what to tell his father. Lars, the landlord's son, suggested they say the pump had simply worn out with age. Noor, whose family rented the farmhouse, pointed out that he had run it dry all afternoon to fill a swimming trough. He argued that the truth would only get her father blamed for poor upkeep. By evening, they had written three versions of the story, each a little more careful than the last, and Noor insisted they keep the one that named Lars. He read it twice, then signed it. Overhead, the bare apricot branches clicked together in the wind like loose shutters.
6bc537ff-ed02-4bd8-8fa3-03daeb6fb694: Urban epidemiologists tracking the spread of cholera in nineteenth-century London relied heavily on maps that plotted individual cases of illness against the locations of public water pumps. One investigator noticed that cases clustered tightly around a single pump on Broad Street, while a nearby brewery, whose workers drank almost exclusively beer brewed on-site rather than water from the pump, reported almost no cases among its employees despite being situated in the same neighborhood. When the handle of the Broad Street pump was removed, new cases in the surrounding area dropped sharply within days. Taken together, these observations suggest that the brewery workers' low infection rate was primarily attributable to ______
3caab309-8fda-4357-ae87-80f613c96cee: Promises cost money. Aunt Consuelo said so every evening as she counted the day's coins at their food cart on the promenade in Oaxaca, and Tomoe, sixteen and tired of hearing it, had stopped arguing. That afternoon Tomoe had told a small boy, who lingered by the cart without a peso, that she would save him a tamal at closing. Consuelo had overheard and clicked her tongue. Now the sun was sinking into the Pacific, the last tamal sat wrapped in its husk, and a customer was holding out a bill for it. Consuelo took the tamal from the steamer, looked down the promenade at the boy hurrying toward them, and set it in Tomoe's hands instead. 'A promise is also a debt,' she said quietly, and for once she did not count anything.
33131ace-474b-4b40-8a77-8a97f73d939c: Marine biologists studying the deep-sea anglerfish have long puzzled over how males, which are dramatically smaller than females and lack the ability to hunt effectively, manage to survive long enough to reproduce in the vast, food-scarce darkness of the ocean. Some anglerfish species solve this problem through sexual parasitism: upon encountering a female, a male permanently fuses his body to hers, and over time their tissues merge until he loses his eyes, fins, and internal organs, surviving only as a source of sperm nourished by her bloodstream. Researchers have observed that in species where males retain independent, fully functional digestive systems throughout adulthood, this permanent fusion behavior is absent. Given this pattern, researchers suspect that the evolution of permanent fusion in certain anglerfish species is most directly linked to ______
8f0ada5b-ea50-46ea-84df-1eefa5e90fba: In surveys of small freshwater ponds in the Netherlands, ecologist Marit Hoekstra found that ponds with dense stands of submerged stonewort algae (Chara) also tended to have unusually clear water, whereas ponds lacking stonewort were typically murky with floating phytoplankton. Hoekstra hypothesizes that stonewort actively causes the clarity: she proposes that the algae release chemical compounds that suppress phytoplankton growth. Skeptics note, however, that stonewort needs abundant light to establish on pond bottoms, so it may simply be that stonewort thrives only in ponds that are already clear for other reasons.
e8977a70-dc8f-42ea-b3ee-7c0da1de9fc4:

- It was redesigned by Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí between 1904 and 1906.

34a8cf11-96c6-4c1b-baf5-9a0d210a9c79: Urban planners in several mid-sized cities have proposed converting underused downtown parking garages into mixed-use residential buildings as a way to address housing shortages. cbd5be11-80d5-4daf-a9b9-106b693a6f41:
Text 1
Art historian Beatrice Dumont attributes the sudden shift toward looser brushwork in late nineteenth-century French painting primarily to the influence of Japanese woodblock prints, which flooded Parisian markets after trade routes opened. Dumont argues that painters like those associated with Impressionism directly borrowed compositional techniques—flattened perspective, cropped framing, and bold color blocks—from these imported prints, making Japanese art the decisive catalyst for the movement's stylistic break from academic tradition.

Text 2
Art historian Julien Fontaine acknowledges that Japanese prints circulated widely among Parisian artists but insists that the technical innovations enabling Impressionism originated earlier, with the invention of portable paint tubes that allowed painters to work outdoors and capture fleeting effects of natural light. Fontaine maintains that this practical, material innovation—not any particular foreign artistic influence—gave painters the freedom to experiment with spontaneous brushwork well before Japanese prints became widely available in Paris.
1ac4e5b2-9bd9-41d7-ac24-801bc90269d9: Art historians examining a newly restored fresco noticed that the original painter had left certain figures deliberately unfinished, their outlines sketched but never filled with pigment. Rather than viewing this as evidence of an interrupted commission, the lead conservator argued that the incompleteness was <u>calculated</u>: comparing the fresco to preliminary drawings found in the artist's workshop, she showed that the same figures appeared unfinished in three separate studies, each time in the same pose. The consistency, she concluded, pointed to an intentional artistic choice rather than an accident of circumstance.
2ddbdc76-0e3c-429f-acff-2d246f44aaf4: Mangrove forests grow along tropical coastlines, where their thick, tangled roots slow down incoming waves. During storms, these roots absorb much of the water's force before it reaches the shore. ______ villages located behind healthy mangrove forests often suffer far less flood damage than villages on unprotected coasts.
f10f0be0-a419-4ceb-b25f-0e5b6839697c: Urban planners redesigning the Riverside Transit Corridor faced a persistent bottleneck at its central interchange______buses idled for nearly fifteen minutes during peak hours while waiting for a single traffic signal to cycle.
eac2f683-39d9-40bc-b289-161597f5a690:
Who pays a clockmaker for the hours he gives away?
On Forty-Third Street my father, Santiago,
kept every clock in the window five minutes fast
so passersby would think themselves late and hurry in.
Ottavio came in January with his wife's watch,
mainspring snapped, the crystal fogged like breath on glass.
He laid his nickels out in a careful row.
My father slid them back across the counter
and bent above the bench past closing, past supper,
lending the stranger his own evening,
asking nothing on account.
I translated nothing. Nothing needed saying.
When the small heart started, Ottavio wept in Italian;
my father answered him in Spanish.
Neither man asked when the debt would come due.
I stood between them holding my English,
the one who believed words were the price of things.
40117e80-c220-4e7b-b3b0-152d54187a7c: Warm celluloid and machine oil: that smell still returns to me whenever it rains. In the projection booth of the old cinema in Kerala, Rajendra taught Zeynep to splice film without saying more than a dozen words a night. They had been friends since childhood, and talk had long ago become unnecessary between them. He would hold a strip up to the bulb, and she would nod; he would press the cement, and she would count the seconds under her breath. Everyone in town said that soon no theater would need such hands, and some nights the empty seats below seemed to agree. Yet the two of them worked as though each careful join were a promise. Rain drummed on the corrugated roof, and a bat slipped out through the vent.
8a9ed576-2730-4661-9ce1-d4d7cbdfd3b7: Urban planners in Bogotá redesigned the city's bus rapid transit corridors to reduce congestion during peak commuting hours. a39efb3e-8669-45a2-8181-bd39c5746815: The octopus's ability to change both the color and texture of its skin almost instantaneously has long fascinated biologists. Specialized cells called chromatophores allow the animal to shift pigment patterns within a fraction of a second, producing camouflage that matches complex backgrounds such as coral or rocky seafloor. ______ the octopus lacks the neural architecture that would allow it to consciously perceive the colors it is mimicking, since octopus photoreceptors are concentrated almost entirely in the skin rather than centralized in a color-processing visual cortex like that of many vertebrates.
77f9998e-0aab-4fb8-bb22-964b05878293: When engineers at a Dutch firm designed a pedestrian bridge from 3D-printed stainless steel, they expected the printing process to be the project's main obstacle: depositing molten metal layer by layer over a 12-meter span had never been attempted. The robotic printers, however, completed the structure in about six months with few interruptions. ______ the greater difficulty came afterward, when inspectors had to certify a material whose internal grain structure differed from that of conventionally rolled steel and for which no existing safety codes applied.
841e2bab-63df-4b65-8343-32f3f139a782: Botanists studying carnivorous plants have long noted that species such as the Venus flytrap grow in nutrient-poor, boggy soils where nitrogen and phosphorus are scarce, yet these plants still manage to photosynthesize normally and produce flowers. For decades, researchers assumed that trapping and digesting insects served primarily to supplement the plant's energy needs, much like an animal eating food for fuel. Careful chemical analysis, however, has shown that captured insects contribute almost no usable carbohydrates or energy to the plant; instead, the digested insects supply nitrogen and phosphorus that the plant cannot extract from its impoverished soil. This distinction matters because it reframes carnivory in plants not as an alternative energy strategy but as a specialized method of nutrient acquisition that allows the plant to compensate for a mineral-poor environment while still relying on sunlight for energy.
d3bfd471-47d9-42a7-ac3b-4ffe69890444: For decades, textbooks described the Pacific lamprey as a primitive nuisance, a jawless parasite whose decline in Columbia River tributaries mattered little except to the salmon it fed upon. Fisheries managers accordingly focused dam passage designs on salmon alone, and few surveys even counted lampreys. Ecologist Laurel Okafor ______ this view in her 2021 synthesis, arguing that lamprey larvae, which filter organic matter from riverbed sediments for years before migrating, recycle nutrients so extensively that their disappearance alters the food supply of the very salmon they were once thought merely to harm.
0bbdf3c0-b0ea-45f2-8a19-8c482cdfc192:
Text 1

Marine biologists studying coral bleaching argue that rising ocean temperatures are the primary driver of reef decline worldwide. In field surveys across the Pacific, reefs exposed to unusually warm water for even a few weeks showed dramatic loss of the symbiotic algae that give coral its color and nutrients. Because these thermal events are becoming more frequent as global temperatures rise, the researchers conclude that curbing greenhouse gas emissions is the most urgent step for reef conservation, since local protections alone cannot shield coral from basin-wide warming trends.

Text 2

Other researchers who study reef ecosystems caution against focusing solely on temperature. Their surveys of reefs near coastal cities found that bleaching was often worst where runoff from agriculture and sewage had already stressed coral with excess nutrients and pollutants. In their view, coral weakened by poor water quality bleaches at lower temperatures than healthy coral would, so improving local water quality could make reefs more resilient to warming even before global emissions are addressed.
0cf57c09-cb27-4166-9f90-10d260c961e5: The Vela satellites, launched by the United States during the 1960s, were originally designed to detect atmospheric nuclear tests, but their sensors unexpectedly recorded brief bursts of gamma radiation from deep space. Astronomers eventually realized that these signals came not from any terrestrial source but from cataclysmic events far beyond the solar system, ______ the field of gamma-ray burst astronomy.
eed938f0-ce8d-4637-9ca4-5bf3fef02fdd: During the early twentieth century, many city governments in the United States widened streets and removed streetcar tracks to accommodate the growing number of automobiles. This shift favored private car ownership over shared transit and reduced the space available for pedestrians. ______ several cities are now narrowing streets and reinstalling rail lines to encourage walking and public transportation.
38ba552f-120c-40a0-a4ce-c556836c30e3: When Remy arrived at the community garden in Marseille, Noemie was already kneeling among the basil, a notebook open on the soil beside her. For years Remy had owed her uncle money, and her uncle had owed him something too: the fish stew he had cooked at every festival but never written down. Since the funeral, Noemie had asked about the stew twice, each time stopping before she said why. Today Remy did not mention the debt. Instead he pinched a leaf of fennel, named it, and waited while she wrote. Then he named the saffron, the orange peel, the bay. Noemie's pencil moved faster, and she did not look up. Afterward he helped her carry the watering cans to the shed and latched its rusty door.
826d1ecc-ce49-4a72-aa7d-714c75d5f1a9: Salt keeps nothing secret. On the flats outside Marrakesh it shows every footprint, every drag of a rake, and so the whole crew saw Malek stop when Lindiwe arrived with the old rake-master's wooden rake on her shoulder. She was nineteen, three weeks on the job, and the old man's granddaughter; the rake had come to her in his will. Malek assigned her the farthest pan and said nothing about it. __When he took off his gloves at noon, the ridges across his palms matched, groove for groove, the worn places on that handle, where for twenty years he had pulled it beside the old man.__ Lindiwe noticed. She worked the far pan until dusk, then walked back across the white crust and leaned the rake against Malek's shed. It pulls left, she told him. You will know how to correct it. He did not thank her, but the next morning he moved her pan closer to his own.
c9e502d1-3c3d-4600-822b-056a5b0fd17f:
Many historians of medieval Iceland have treated the family sagas as unreliable guides to the era they describe. Because the sagas were written down in the thirteenth century, roughly three hundred years after the settlement-era feuds they narrate, these scholars argue that the texts mainly reflect the political anxieties of their thirteenth-century authors, and that any resemblance to earlier events is largely coincidental.

Archaeologist Hrefna Jónsdóttir has excavated several farmsteads named in the sagas. At a number of them, she found that the layout of buildings, the approximate dates of their construction, and even the positions of boundary walls match saga descriptions closely. At the same sites, however, she found no physical evidence of the large feasting halls or wealth that the sagas attribute to their owners, details Jónsdóttir attributes to later writers magnifying the status of their ancestors.
658d1461-18fc-424e-be9a-198df6f4ad69: Ink, hot metal, and the steady thud of the flatbed: I still smell and hear the press room in Mumbai whenever Sergio telephones. We set type side by side there for nine years before he moved to Goa, and he still calls me, Ishaan, his apprentice, though I outlasted him by a decade. Last week he rang about our old foreman, who is dying and keeps asking whether the shop he founded still runs. It does not; it closed in 1994. Sergio thinks we should tell him the truth. I keep picturing the foreman tapping each line of type with his thumb, proud as a father, and I am not sure what I will say. Still, I laughed when Sergio reminded me how I once printed a wedding card with the groom's name upside down. My neighbor's radio is playing an old film song through the wall.
6eed1b91-670c-4df9-9306-a07d2dde2bd0: Rain beaded on the manuscript pages Jiayi had carried to the stone bridge, and she shielded them with her sleeve while Haoran read. He had translated four of her novels and liked to say that he read her endings first, the way some people taste the sauce before the noodles. Tonight he lingered over the opening chapters, laughing aloud at a scene in a fish market and quoting a line about a stubborn aunt back to her twice. Jiayi teased him for performing, and he bowed to the lanterns as if they were an audience. When he reached the last pages, he read them quickly, squared the stack, and began to tell her about a noodle shop that had opened behind the temple. She waited for the joke about the sauce. He offered her the pages instead, holding them by the corners so the rain would not spot the final chapter, the one she had rewritten six times. Traffic hissed over the wet stones. Jiayi tucked the manuscript under her coat and asked, in an even voice, whether the shop stayed open late.
4b8a71ee-155d-42ad-8def-2c3eff9a2ec8: When the monsoon filled our cellar in Karachi, my twin, Nadeesha, and I had been dividing our late father's house for two months without once mentioning why he had left it to us in equal halves. We split the furniture by alternating choices, the books by shelf, the kitchen by drawer. Every list was polite and complete, and none of it touched the subject. The flood made lists useless. We waded in together, passing up boxes neither of us had labeled, and in one of them were letters he had written to each of us and never sent. We read them sitting on the stairs, our feet still in the water, and for the first time that year we argued, loudly, about him. By evening the pump had begun its slow work, coughing brown water into the lane.

- Lina Bo Bardi was an Italian-born Brazilian architect.

a664a8d0-7ccf-44c0-adc7-9092bee7da11:
When Sepeli dropped both pig and Chancellor, a talking man from the windward coast picked up the carcass. Cornelius was on his feet and running, when the pig caught him on the legs and tripped him. The people and the army, with shouts and laughter, joined in the sport.

Twist and dodge as he would, everywhere the ex-Chancellor of the Exchequer was met or overtaken by the flying pig. He scuttled like a frightened rabbit in and out among the avocados and the palms. No hand was laid upon him, and his tormentors made way before him, but ever they pursued, and ever the pig flew as fast as hands could pick it up.
d7fc03eb-05f1-4b54-8d40-2dd06152ddd0: Three clothespins per shirt, two per towel, one per sock: Ximena had hung her family's laundry by these rules on the Cairo rooftop since she was eight. Tariq, the landlord's son, liked to watch her count them out from the stairwell. One afternoon the wind came hard off the desert, and he ran up to help, pinning sheets any way he could, sometimes with four pins, sometimes with none. Ximena nearly scolded him. Instead she watched the sheets snap and hold, and she noticed that not one had fallen. The next week she left a few towels hanging by a single pin, just to see. They dried as quickly as the others. Below the roof, a vendor called out the price of guavas, and pigeons settled in a row along the water tank.
a83ecd0e-9884-4c22-8395-09e62f0f4abb: During the 1970s stagflation, many economists expected that rising unemployment would, as traditional models predicted, come paired with falling inflation. Instead, the United States experienced both high unemployment and high inflation simultaneously, a combination the standard Phillips curve could not explain. ______ economists began incorporating inflation expectations into their models, arguing that once workers and firms expect prices to keep rising, wage and price increases become self-reinforcing regardless of unemployment levels.
7880e283-b164-4ab4-9ad1-128abdc70ae2: Wind hissed through the pines above the mountain bus stop near Porto Alegre, and my mother, Mingyu, smelled of the orange peel she chews when she is deciding something. Our family rule had come down from her grandmother, who married in a valley town with two roads to the chapel: a bride must not see the wedding road before the wedding day. I was the bride, Booker was the groom, and up here there was exactly one road, which every bus took. My mother read the timetable twice, then folded it into a small square. Rules are coats, she said, and her own mother's had been let out twice before it ever reached her. She tucked the timetable into my pocket, and when the bus came, she climbed on beside me without looking away from the road.
16315955-d50a-4a40-bc56-0c90f8b9372b: We split the house our mother left us the way she had taught us to split a bolt of cloth at the weaving cooperative: measure twice, cut once, argue never. Marcus took the kitchen and the back porch. I took the front rooms and the loom. When the cooperative's director called to say that Marcus's quilt had been chosen for the state museum, he shrugged into the phone and said it was just scraps. He told me the same thing that night, twice, while we taped boxes. He said the museum probably needed something to fill a wall. __Yet when he packed the quilt to send it, he folded it so that the little muslin tag stitched with his name lay on top, square in the center, where anyone opening the box would see it first.__ I did not mention it. I only wrote fragile on the box in my best letters, and let him think I had not noticed.
35b9a103-ca63-4efd-b452-d08769d4868b: Ecologists long assumed that the bright orange coloration of the cinnabar moth caterpillar served mainly to warn birds that the insect is toxic, since the caterpillars store bitter alkaloids from the ragwort plants they eat. When biologist Tamsin Hale offered the caterpillars to captive starlings, many birds did reject them after a single taste. ______ a substantial number of starlings that had never encountered the caterpillars avoided them on sight, even when the caterpillars had been rinsed of most of their alkaloids, suggesting that the color itself, rather than learned distaste alone, can deter some predators.
c721984d-05ad-4c46-8c3f-0a2d10fe677d: A civil engineer measured the water flow rate, in gallons per minute, from a set of five showerhead models during a standardized test. The results were as follows: Model A, 1.8 gallons per minute; Model B, 2.3 gallons per minute; Model C, 1.2 gallons per minute; Model D, 2.8 gallons per minute; Model E, 2.0 gallons per minute.
29f6ca2a-1aa0-4799-a320-1e42968f5975: Traditional accounts of the fall of the Western Roman Empire emphasize external pressure from invading groups along the empire's borders. 66b5c96e-5f67-4cfe-a8bc-4feb82fb366e: I fancy we are most of us tired of Constantinople. To me it is a place where a little sight-seeing goes a long way. Our gallant captain, on the contrary, tells me that he could put in three months here very well. As it is, there are about 2,000 English here, to say nothing of naturalized Greeks and Maltese. I suppose Constantinople is not a bad place for a short residence. The hotels are good, and in some you may have a bedroom for four francs a day. Provisions are not dear, but house-rent is very expensive. The population of the place is dense, at which I wonder, as Constantinople seems to me the most unhealthy city I have ever seen.
0921f31c-7ca8-4bda-9b00-4c46dea2b564:
The Suffolk (was it Surrey?) flirt
Without a pang threw over
Poor Jack and all his works like dirt,
And caught a richer lover.

We read one morning more to say
We had not been quite idle,
And then to end the arduous day
Enjoyed a swim in Rydal.

Next day the hundredweight of books
Was packed once more in cases,
We left the lakes and hills and brooks
And southward turned our faces.
a05743e6-6fa1-4b3a-8ac7-164d84c45e9d: Off the coast of Portugal, marine biologist Ana Ferreira has documented an unusual partnership in shallow kelp forests. The decorator crab Pisa armata, a slow-moving species that divers often overlook, attaches living sponges to its shell for camouflage______ the sponges gain access to food particles that the crab stirs up as it walks across the seafloor.
44a8e0b0-75b6-41c6-8a1d-648a5ab3ebf5: Ecologist Mariko Tanaka spent three summers tracking the American pika, a small, round-eared relative of rabbits that lives on rocky alpine slopes ______ data suggest that the animals survive hot afternoons by retreating deep into cool gaps beneath the boulders.
6ad4f9cb-078b-4a56-b407-cbe34b69ba65: In spite of this, the landlord has done his share; chiefly perhaps by yielding--not always gracefully--when it was no longer of any use to fight. There have been exceptions, however: men and women who have mended and built with an eye to the real welfare of their tenants as well as to their own pockets. Let it be well understood that the two are inseparable, if any good is to come of it. The business of housing the poor, if it is to amount to anything, must be business, as it was business with our fathers to put them where they are. As charity, pastime, or fad, it will miserably fail, always and everywhere.
6f9f27c9-ca35-4f65-83f5-0e74223a6900: Urban historians studying the redesign of Seoul's bus rapid transit corridors in the early 2000s have argued that dedicating center-lane bus corridors, rather than curbside lanes, was the single most important factor in reducing average commute times along major arterial roads. aad62b17-cb3a-4352-bea3-2dd2217315d9: Who pays a tutor in oranges? Miriam had asked this aloud the first week, when Fiorella refused her envelope of coins and accepted only a sack of fruit from the barge's hold. Since then the tutor had come every Thursday, climbing down the ladder with her books wrapped against the river damp, and Miriam's brother had begun reading the cargo lists to the crew with sudden pride. Miriam kept the coins in a tin, telling herself she would insist next time. But this evening she found her brother's old shoes, the pair that had split at the toe, replaced by a sturdy one, with a note in Fiorella's handwriting tucked inside: outgrown by my nephew. Miriam set the tin back on its shelf, unopened. Along the bank, a crane swung a pallet of cement toward a waiting truck.
29e03f09-61b6-4996-a845-1727dc7a251f: Intending to engrave the name later in the afternoon, I wrote it down in my order-book, and asked the lady for her address, so that I might send the chain to her the next day. But, no; she would not leave it. She must have the name engraved at once, right away, and must put the necklace herself on her little daughter. She would wait. Ah, how it all comes back to me! Well, I wished to obey the lady, and so set to work. But I saw immediately there was not space enough for the whole name. She was very sorry, poor lady, and then she said I should put on the two letters D. R. There they are, you see, my own work--you see that? And she paid me, and locked the chain on the baby's neck again--ah me! it is so strange!--and she went away.
457fb5e7-a54d-4017-a867-5c425fbbbfc4: When Zofia climbed to the roof that last evening in Thessaloniki, her father was already kneeling beside the water tank, a tin of sealant open at his knee. For eleven summers the tank had wept a thin rust-colored line down the wall, and for eleven summers he had said he would fix it next week. Eda, from the next roof, used to joke that the stain was older than Zofia's English. Zofia had stopped noticing it, the way she had stopped noticing that he never asked about the school prize ceremony he had missed. b508909d-82cb-4caf-ae0b-d437947f0d52: The Antikythera mechanism, an ancient Greek device recovered from a shipwreck in 1901, has long puzzled historians of science. Text 1
Honey bees are essential pollinators of crops, but their impact on wild bee populations has become a growing concern. When managed honey bee hives are placed near natural habitats, honey bees often outcompete native wild bees for pollen and nectar. Because honey bees forage in large numbers and can travel considerable distances, they can quickly deplete floral resources that wild bees depend on for survival. Several studies have found that wild bee abundance declines in areas with high densities of honey bee hives, suggesting that beekeeping practices intended to support agriculture may inadvertently harm native pollinator communities.

Text 2
Concerns about honey bees displacing wild bees often overlook the scale at which beekeeping actually occurs. Most managed hives are placed in or near agricultural fields, not in the untouched natural habitats where sensitive wild bee species live. Furthermore, many wild bee declines predate the recent expansion of commercial beekeeping and are more plausibly linked to pesticide exposure and habitat loss from land development. Blaming honey bees for wild bee declines risks diverting attention and resources away from these more significant and well-documented threats.

b2829d7c-6878-46b4-ac03-3fd3acf2ef2d: Art historians examining Baroque still-life paintings have noted the artists' extraordinary skill at capturing texture, from the dewy skin of grapes to the metallic sheen of silver goblets. 2d0accc8-6926-4e9d-a6d2-26380c0293b7: Textile conservators restoring a collection of nineteenth-century embroidered tapestries were initially puzzled by faint discoloration patterns that appeared only along the edges of certain panels. 0c4fba18-058f-4d21-ba7e-758370c1a264:
Text 1
Marine biologists studying octopus cognition have documented that octopuses can learn to open jars, navigate mazes, and even recognize individual human faces after repeated exposure. Given these abilities, some researchers argue that octopuses possess a form of intelligence comparable to that of many vertebrates, despite having a nervous system that evolved along an entirely separate path from mammals and birds. These researchers contend that intelligence is not a single evolutionary inheritance but something that can arise independently whenever an organism faces sufficiently complex environmental challenges, such as evading predators or manipulating tools to obtain food.

Text 2
While octopuses undeniably perform impressive tasks in laboratory settings, comparing their cognition to that of vertebrates risks obscuring a crucial distinction: roughly two-thirds of an octopus's neurons reside in its arms rather than its central brain, allowing each arm to process sensory information and initiate movement with considerable autonomy. This decentralized architecture suggests that octopus problem-solving may not reflect unified, centralized reasoning at all, but rather a distributed process unlike anything found in vertebrate brains. Treating octopus behavior as evidence of vertebrate-like intelligence may therefore mislead researchers about how cognition actually operates in these animals.
68f11a7d-316e-4870-8262-0c56b644ccd6: The museum's new exhibit traces how a single technique, chiaroscuro, transformed European painting during the Renaissance. c7db54fc-26cd-4965-a891-94edbb5f4691: Economic historians note that the invention of the mechanical clock in medieval Europe did more than help monks keep track of prayer times. 3bdf8705-9e63-4fca-a55f-b155c761df7c: Who remembers a borrowed tablecloth for nine years? Yaa did, apparently. 50635297-9ab4-4437-b505-5c0b4d4a6ec7: Entomologists studying the desert-dwelling Namib beetle (Onymacris unguicularis) have long known that the insect collects drinking water by tilting its body into the wind on fog-laden mornings, allowing droplets to condense on its bumpy back and roll down grooves toward its mouth. d07ca7d3-eec2-4221-bdd6-7fbca6489315: Two rules governed the salt flat behind the house I rented outside Port of Spain: never walk on a pan that is still drying, and never rake against the wind. I have spent years since retelling that drive, and I always slow down at the part where he raked so carefully for a man who would never see the sale.
e5d0f48d-a795-48c6-9c1a-cd3c190b1d60:
Text 1

Urban planners who favor congestion pricing argue that charging drivers a fee to enter crowded downtown areas is the most effective way to reduce traffic. Cities that have adopted such fees report measurable drops in car volume within months, along with faster bus speeds and lower emissions. Because the fee applies immediately and adjusts driver behavior directly, proponents view it as a quicker solution than waiting years for new transit lines or road expansions to be built.

Text 2

Critics of congestion pricing contend that the policy places an unfair burden on lower-income commuters who cannot easily switch to costly alternatives. In cities where public transit remains limited, they note, the fee may simply push struggling drivers to less convenient routes rather than off the road entirely. These critics argue that investing in affordable transit expansion first would reduce car dependence more equitably, even though such projects take longer to complete than implementing a pricing fee.
06e82de4-ba40-4b14-8430-78a847a9a9f6: A sleep researcher studying nocturnal rodent behavior claimed that exposure to artificial light at night disrupts the internal circadian clocks of wild mice, leading them to forage at suboptimal times when predators are more active. ac06885e-849c-4f11-8883-99aaf5577fd9: The axolotl, a salamander native to a small network of lakes near Mexico City, has long fascinated biologists for its ability to regenerate entire limbs, portions of its spinal cord, and even parts of its heart without scarring. Unlike most amphibians, axolotls retain juvenile features such as external gills throughout their adult lives, a trait known as neoteny. Researchers initially studied the species mainly to understand this unusual developmental arrest, but attention has increasingly shifted toward the cellular mechanisms behind its regenerative capacity, since unraveling how axolotl cells avoid forming scar tissue could inform treatments for human injuries that currently heal only through scarring. As a result, laboratories that once focused narrowly on developmental biology now dedicate significant resources to mapping the genetic pathways that allow such complete tissue restoration.
d78a107b-acb8-4bf3-917e-031c2dfc2867: Dongsik mended nets on the Busan pier while Rania read Korean aloud from a child's workbook. When she stumbled over a word for sorry, he corrected her without looking up, then repeated it twice, more softly, as if testing it himself. Every evening she asked whether she could read it to him yet, and every evening he said her vowels were still too American. Tonight, though, he slid the envelope across the crate between them and tapped one line with a tar-stained finger. Read only this part, he said. Rania bent over the paper, sounding out each syllable. 39b35c30-d64a-43a3-95f1-96af2f226625: For decades, ecologists assumed that the tiny freshwater crustacean Daphnia grows protective neck spines only when it detects chemicals released by predatory midge larvae. Yet when biologist Maren Holt surveyed ponds in which the larvae had been absent for years, she still found spined Daphnia in several of them. __Holt noticed that every one of these ponds lay downstream of a pond where the larvae remained abundant.__ Testing water carried from the upstream ponds, she detected the larval cue at low but measurable levels, suggesting that the chemical signal can travel between connected ponds and that the spines she observed were not, after all, evidence against the original hypothesis.
3517d1e1-7731-4210-9c88-211e1bb6ad51: Written in spare contemporary prose but steeped in the gaslit gloom of a Victorian novel, Mara Ellison's The Lamplighter's Daughter unfolds through a single recollecting voice. d7808f28-9b34-4d88-af5d-6226fe36a0d6: For decades, historians of ancient trade assumed that the Roman glass industry was a marginal craft practiced by a handful of workshops near the imperial capital. This view rested largely on the scarcity of glass artifacts recovered from provincial sites compared with pottery and metalwork. Recent chemical analyses of glass fragments from sites across the former empire, however, have revealed a striking uniformity in raw material composition, suggesting that glass was manufactured at only a few coastal centers, such as those in the Levant and Egypt, and then shipped as raw chunks to secondary workshops throughout the Mediterranean for local shaping into finished vessels. __This division between primary production and secondary finishing, rather than a lack of overall output, explains why so few large glassmaking furnaces have been found far from the coast: most inland workshops never produced raw glass at all, and so left behind only the smaller tools used for reheating and shaping imported material.__ The finding suggests that the industry was in fact vast and highly organized, coordinating specialized production across enormous distances long before such logistical networks were thought possible.
60f58fb7-7718-467a-b3bb-f6b9d4d70a9c: Botanists studying carnivorous pitcher plants have traditionally explained their insect-trapping pitchers as adaptations for acquiring nitrogen and other nutrients scarce in the boggy, acidic soils where these plants typically grow. Recent field observations of several pitcher plant species, however, have complicated this straightforward explanation. Researchers found that some pitchers host thriving communities of mosquito larvae, midge larvae, and bacteria that survive within the digestive fluid, apparently unharmed by the enzymes that dissolve other trapped insects. Rather than functioning purely as passive traps, these pitchers appear to operate as miniature ecosystems in which certain organisms process captured prey into forms of nitrogen the plant can more easily absorb, effectively acting as intermediaries in digestion. This has led some researchers to propose that at least some pitcher plant species depend on these resident communities as much as on their own digestive enzymes to obtain nutrients.
47d3837b-1354-4d1b-9f8b-1b810d9c3357: Economists analyzing the collapse of the Bretton Woods monetary system in the early 1970s have generally focused on the decision by the United States to suspend the dollar's convertibility into gold, a move that effectively ended the fixed exchange rate arrangement that had governed international trade since World War II. Some scholars argue that this shift primarily reflected mounting inflationary pressures within the American economy. ______ other researchers point to the growing volume of dollars held overseas, which made the fixed peg increasingly difficult for the United States to sustain regardless of its domestic inflation rate.
0cb742bc-a60c-472b-a45f-3e86dc8e166f:

BARTOLO: I drafted three hundred pages of that opinion. You know I did.
LAN: (still amused) And I signed them. That is how it is done, my boy.
BARTOLO: My father is buried here. I promised him our family name would mean something one day. (He holds out the paper.) Read it to him.

e4ee863c-a6c8-4337-a479-76bfb7e9814f: Indeed, I fancy it is one of the most interesting cities in France. 963147be-0d6f-4579-a985-fda1f1ff9783: For decades, marine biologists assumed that octopuses were solitary creatures with little capacity for social behavior, since most species observed in the wild tend to avoid one another outside of mating. While the octopuses were not cooperating in the way that highly social animals like dolphins do, their behavior at the site was far more complex and communicative than the strictly solitary model had predicted. Tam would have come into it almost intact. He might have been able to educate himself while he was yet young, to spare himself many a drudging day and weary night.

1b3d0130-1471-46c3-b4f9-815e86cddc36: There are some people who habitually, and from a strong sense of duty, live on the shady side of life. and the crust is soft as an excuse.
I say it to the counter, to the coffee,
to the road outside where the trucks don't stop.
Felix would have shouted. Felix kept
a ledger of every coin you took that spring
before you learned to knock instead of climb.
I am not keeping one, or not exactly;
I only know the number by heart.
Mornings, I leave the side door on the latch.
I set the second cup out on the counter,
the one with the chipped blue rim,
and pour it before your engine reaches the hill.
When you come in shaking rain from your collar,

and push the old ledger, unopened, under the till.
2196f74f-289b-4cfd-b7e4-f19282d48226: Art historians examining the Dutch Golden Age have often focused on the grand history paintings and formal portraits commissioned by wealthy patrons, treating still-life paintings of flowers, fruit, and household objects as decorative works of secondary importance. Recent scholarship, however, has revealed that these still lifes frequently contained coded references to mortality, economic anxiety, and moral caution that would have been immediately legible to seventeenth-century Dutch viewers. A wilting flower or an overturned glass, for instance, was widely understood as a reminder of life's fragility, while an unusually exotic imported fruit could signal both prosperity and the moral peril of excessive luxury. By recovering this visual vocabulary, historians have repositioned still-life painting as a genre engaged with the same intellectual and social concerns as history painting, rather than a lesser tradition concerned only with surface appearance.
1c3d5e2c-cbe2-4a89-9e05-215fe2082301: In 1974, astronomers Russell Hulse and Joseph Taylor discovered a pulsar locked in a tight orbit with a companion neutron star. When the looms of the Tbilisi weaving cooperative fall silent each evening, I set two chairs by the window, and Anushka begins on the tangled yarn the weavers leave behind. We used to play here on Fridays; now nobody asks.

IRENA: (after a pause) Practice, maybe.
ANUSHKA: Practice for whom?
(IRENA reaches for her violin case. ANUSHKA slides the spool across first, so that IRENA holds one end while she winds.)

The hot, sleepy streets were waking up in the red glow of the fading day. People in the town, now that the glare had died from their eyes, were telling each other that the air was cool, and trying to believe it.

Outside, however, the assertion had more truth in it. A ripple of refreshment was slowly spreading up from the distant river. The shadows of the straight-lined trees lay across the brick road in great black stripes. The girls walked on in silence till they reached a point where the road swerved off into a little thicket. This was the spot which Romeo must have had in his mind.
e99c754f-6e64-4086-a5da-2af9450083f3: When Rangi arrived at the hospital in Wailuku, his twin, Anahera, had already claimed the chair nearest the nurses' desk, a clipboard of their father's forms on his knee. Rangi had assumed the answer for years: the brother who never left would simply keep staying. But watching Anahera's thumb worry the edge of the clipboard, he saw how tired that brother was. 834aef0c-57c7-4956-8876-fbf035963550: Urban planners in the mid-twentieth century widely embraced the construction of elevated highways as a solution to traffic congestion in dense cities. 0a18ec33-1337-4fe1-a958-a6feaaec1b7f: Minjun found the gift on the shared wall between their yards on Jeju Island: a jar of honey, labeled in Younghee's careful hand, tied with red string. 39347998-add8-4c5c-8695-3d611d6a0e7c: Marine biologists studying octopus cognition have long been puzzled by the animals' capacity to solve novel problems despite having no contact with their parents, who die shortly after reproducing. 3c5d4dd3-2fc8-47ba-8a37-c4c4a687140e: Three things never changed on my route: the pothole by the market, the fare, and Kemoy stepping off at Charlotte Street with the same two words, Later, driver. e1d85626-a1dd-4bfb-95a3-4a960b583ebe:
When the boats come in at dawn to the harbor in Hanoi,
the rule is old: the tenants' catch is weighed first,
and the landlord's scale is always kind to the landlord.
Everyone obeys. My father obeys. I, Aoife, obey,
my hands smelling of salt and silence.
But this morning Somchai, the landlord's son,
stood at the scale and read the true weight aloud,
loud enough for the gulls, loud enough for the nets.
My heart knocked like a hull against the pier,
afraid of what his father would say,
and still I lifted my basket higher
so the whole dock could see the numbers.
Somewhere a bell rang for the market.
A woman sold green mangoes from a bicycle,
and the river kept pushing its brown water toward the sea.
ecf24f9d-b0d9-491d-b9c2-8ad188ce9582: For decades, archaeologists assumed that the stone terraces covering the hillsides of Peru's Colca Valley had been abandoned after the Spanish conquest and left to crumble. Text 1

Botanists studying carnivorous pitcher plants argue that their trapping mechanism evolved primarily as an adaptation to nutrient-poor soil, allowing the plants to obtain nitrogen from insect prey that they cannot easily get from the ground. Field studies show that pitcher plants growing in the poorest soils tend to produce the largest, most elaborate traps, supporting the idea that nutrient scarcity directly drives the intensity of carnivorous adaptation.

Text 2

Other botanists note that some pitcher plant traps also host small communities of insect larvae and bacteria that help break down prey, suggesting the traps function less like simple nutrient-scarcity adaptations and more like miniature digestive ecosystems. They argue that trap size and shape may be shaped as much by maintaining these internal communities as by the surrounding soil's nutrient content, complicating any simple link between poor soil and elaborate traps.

5d161d71-43d7-43c9-942e-0c63ed3c5224: By six the kitchen of the boarding house in Manila smelled of garlic rice, and Tyrese was already at the long table with the ledger open.
